x: The "slows," led by Tolley, went about 5 miles, the "mediums," under Gorringe, about 6 miles, and the "speed merchants" 7 miles. It was a very cold afternoon and sweaters (or several vests) were the order of the day.

A large number faced the starter and at his signal all were well away, with Tolley, Epsom, leading and Humphris (S.L.H.) closely following. After waiting some little time they could be seen in the distance and, on reaching me, they had covered about half the way, with Tolley still leading the way.

Tolley and Court took an initial lead, opening up quite a gap but Court later managed to make a break to win comfortably. Len Duquemin and John Moullin were up in the thick of it in the first six for the whole race and at five miles Smallwood was disqualified leaving three Bels in six.
A battle evolved between five competitors; Flynn, Lightman, Tolley, Court and Lawton. This group later split, with Flynn and Lightman breaking away to finish in that order.
